record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: For polygonal billiards, can one classify the ergodic invariant probability measures and the closed invariant subsets?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 33 (A. Katok). Classify the ergodic invariant probability measures and closed invariant subsets for polygonal billiards.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygon (a compact, connected planar region bounded by finitely many line segments). The billiard flow on $P$ is the dynamical system on the unit tangent bundle of $P$ defined by free motion of a point particle inside $P$ with elastic reflection at the boundary (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection), with trajectories meeting a corner of $P$ left undefined. This flow preserves Liouville measure.

Provide a classification of:
(a) all ergodic Borel probability measures invariant under the billiard flow on $P$, and
(b) all closed subsets of the phase space that are invariant under the billiard flow,
in terms of the geometric data of the polygon $P$ (in particular, treating both rational polygons, whose angles are rational multiples of $\pi$, and irrational polygons).
artifact.status_search_result: The general classification of ergodic invariant probability measures and closed invariant sets for polygonal billiards remains open. Partial results exist: for rational polygons the dynamics reduces to translation flows on Veech surfaces where Masur–Veech and subsequent work give substantial information; for irrational polygons even basic questions (e.g., existence of dense orbits, ergodicity of generic polygons, weak mixing) are only partially understood. Recent works address SRB measures under perturbed reflection laws and weak mixing in rational billiards, but no full classification is known.

status_evidence.title: Weakly Mixing Polygonal Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture that for almost all polygonal tables the billiard flow is ergodic and weakly mixing—indicates the classification problem remains unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Fundamental questions about ergodic properties of polygonal billiards remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems from the workshop 'Emerging Applications of Measure Rigidity'
status_evidence.snippet: Lists Katok's question on classifying ergodic invariant measures among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem is recorded as an open problem in the community.

status_evidence.title: Weak mixing in rational billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work on weak mixing in rational polygonal billiards, building toward but not completing classification.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research indicates the problem is not yet fully resolved.
